correctness.rationale: In the Hilbert–Schmidt Weyl basis distinct conjugation characters separate each coefficient of the rank-one seed; each orbit frame eigenvalue is p times the squared modulus of the corresponding ambiguity coefficient. At a=0 these are p−1+t² and t²−1, so the only failure on that axis is t=1. For a≠0 completing the square in 3aj²+(3a²+b)j+a³ and correcting j=0,−a gives the stated Gauss term and (t−1)(1+ζ^(−ab)). After extracting ζ^(−ab/2), the correction is real and its cosine factor is nonzero. For p≡3 mod 4, iζ^k cannot be real; for p≡1 mod 4 reality forces (3a²+b)²/(12a)=ab/2, giving b²+9a⁴=0. Since √p>2, only the displayed sign gives a nonnegative exceptional replacement. Independent modular enumeration gives 0, 0 and 8 sign-admissible pairs at p=5,13,17 respectively. The displayed p=17 amplitude and its decimal are correct; there is a second value at 1+√17/(2cos(6π/17)), which the full formula includes and the wording does not exclude. Direct finite sums at the two p=17 amplitudes corroborate the predicted zeros; the uploaded checker was read but not run. The primary Li passage inspected does not substantiate the corresponding related-work sentence, but that is not used in the theorem.
